name: Tourmaline-Frost
description: Tourmaline-Frost gleams with the multicolored iridescence of its namesake mineral, its ice sheets refracting weak starlight into prismatic bands of pink, green, and electric blue. Methane lakes pool in ancient impact basins, their surfaces so still they appear solid until disturbed. Beneath the frozen crust, a liquid water ocean circulates around a warm rocky core, heated by tidal forces from a nearby gas giant.

The thin atmosphere carries ice crystals that catch the light like suspended glitter, creating halos around any light source. The cold is profound and penetrating, defeating thermal regulation systems within hours of extended surface exposure. Sound travels oddly through the frigid air, arriving muted and delayed, giving the landscape a dreamlike quality.

A research outpost called Prism Station has operated on the surface for twelve years, staffed by astrobiologists studying the microbial ecosystems that thrive in the subterranean ocean. These extremophiles metabolize exotic matter trace elements in ways that challenge fundamental biochemistry. The outpost has also detected anomalous energy signatures deep within the ocean, regular pulses that may be geological or may be something else entirely.

Tourmaline-Frost's exotic matter deposits, though trace, have attracted military interest, as even small quantities have strategic applications. The research team fiercely guards their scientific mandate, but their funding depends on agencies with less academic priorities. The ocean below holds more than microbes, and every bore-hole sample brings the surface closer to whatever waits in the deep.
